 Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs had the perfect play to beat the Broncos. But a flag wiped it all out.  
 Andy Reid and his QB chose their words carefully about the call that left Chiefs Nation stewing and Broncos Country hooting. But Mahomes’ wife didn’t mince words.

 By Nate Peterson | npeterson@denverpost.com | The Denver Post PUBLISHED: November 2, 2026 at 4:00 AM MST | UPDATED: November 2, 2026 at 9:23 AM MST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Fourth-and-1 with 4 ticks to go. The perfect time for Andy Reid to dip into his bag of tricks and pull out a game-winning treat for Patrick Mahomes.
 The Chiefs sent Travis Kelce in motion from right to left, drawing multiple Broncos defenders. At the snap, Rashee Rice slipped under the big tight end and ran a shallow cross, hauling in what looked like an easy game-winning touchdown from Mahomes.
 But a flag on the far right side of the field made it all moot. The call? False start on Kansas City right tackle Jaylon Moore. It was a dead-ball foul, meaning the play never happened and the Chiefs had to back up 5 yards. On fourth-and-goal from the 6, Broncos edge rushers Nik Bonitto and Jonathon Cooper squeezed the pocket, forcing Mahomes right into Malcolm Roach to end the game .
 In two plays, the Chiefs went from being essentially three games up in the AFC West to looking up at the rival Broncos in the division standings.
 Broncos coach Sean Payton credited the raucous crowd of 76,831 Broncomaniacs at Empower Field.
 “Won us the game tonight,” Payton said.
 As for the coach on the opposite sideline, Reid chose his words carefully about the call that wiped out the touchdown.
 “I didn’t see it,” he said. “So … I didn’t think it was big enough. I saw him move his head, but I didn’t see a false start.”
 When pressed to clarify what he did and didn’t see, Reid said: “Yeah, I saw him move his head a little bit. And my eyes went off it after that.”
 Translation: Not enough movement to draw a whistle.

 Mahomes was also deliberate in his word choice.
 “I have not seen it,” he said. “But it didn’t surprise me or catch me or anything like that, so it couldn’t have been big. It was called. At the end of the day, you have to go with whatever is called. But a lot of times, in those big moments, the little stuff doesn’t get called like that.”
 Mahomes’ wife, Brittany, however, didn’t mince words. In a social media post , she called the flag “the weakest call I have ever seen.”
 “You can’t tell me you call that on a game-winning TD,” she wrote. “ … oh wait yeah I can cause it’s us.”
 Chalk it up to another juicy chapter in a Broncos-Chiefs rivalry full of them — from Joe Montana beating John Elway in a “Monday Night Football” classic to Shannon Sharpe getting fellow Hall of Famer Derrick Thomas to snap in another Monday nighter to the infamous “Vaseline Game” that the Broncos won in Kansas City in the two rivals’ only postseason meeting.
 Broncos Country is convinced the Chiefs of Mahomes, Reid, and Kelce have had calls go their way for years, especially since Taylor Swift came into the picture. Chiefs Nation will never be unconvinced that the whistle on Moore is just the latest sign of a “hate us cause they ain’t us” mentality around the league.
 What was clear after the game, however, was that the Chiefs didn’t have another perfect bullet to fire on fourth-and-goal from the 6.
 “We’d kind of showcased that play, we talked about that play in the meeting the night before,” Mahomes said. “You get a lot of attention on Trav and you hit Rashee underneath. That last one, they covered it well. Whenever you get there, and you don’t capitalize, you take that on yourself.”
